newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WESTERN METALS SAYS CONFIDENT ON PILLARA.
newsitem.headline: WESTERN METALS SAYS CONFIDENT ON PILLARA.

text.p: Base metals miner Western Metals Ltd, which operates in the remote Kimberley region of Western Australia, said on Tuesday it was confident that its new Pillara zinc and lead mine would be a low-risk venture.
Western Metals managing director Rod Webster told a base metals conference feasibility studies indicated the venture could be quite profitable.
He said the plant also had potential to increase throughput significantly while a new A$4.5 million barge had been constructed so the group could conduct its own port operations.

The Pillara plant will be commissioned in mid-1998 to treat 1.5 million tonnes of ore a year at a grade cut-off point of five percent zinc. The plant had the potential to increase treatment by between one million tonnes and 1.5 million tonnes a year at a cut-off grade of three percent, Webster said.
The company has renovated the old Derby port, which has been closed for about 12 years, he said.

A new A$4.5 million self-discharging 4,500 tonne capacity barge also would be completed in about one month for commissioning towards the end of 1997, Webster told the conference, sponsored by broker Bell Securities.

The current 12 month period would be the company's most difficult year, with falling grades from existing operations before Pillara came on stream, Webster said. But enormous economies would be able to be achieved with Pillara, he said.
With Pillara in production, Western Metals' Kimberley area, known as Lennard Shelf, would rank as the seventh largest zinc producer in the world in 1999, on 160,000 tonnes of contained zinc, he said.

This would compare with 500,000 tonnes produced by the world's top producer, Cominco Ltd's Red Dog mine in Alaska and 200,000 tonnes by MIM Holdings Ltd's Mount Isa mine in Australia, the third largest producer, he said.
Webster said Western Metals had examined installing a lead smelter in Indonesia but the plan had not advanced as hoped.
